articles.text: Only a finding reproduced by a transaction that succeeds against the program, moving funds to the attacker or handing the attacker an authority, counts toward a Fuzzy Score or a certification. Everything else is a lead: shown, never scored.
A Fuzzy Score is the lower of Depth and the ceiling set by the worst proven finding. No change may let a run with a proven finding score above that finding's ceiling.
A score and a certification name one exact build of a program by its bytecode hash. A new build is uncertified until it is certified again.
A Verafy Certification is written only from a sealed ruling by registered harnesses: at least three seats from at least two model families. Nobody certifies their own program by signing.
Fuzzy never sends a transaction to mainnet or devnet while testing. Attacks run on local copies.
No amendment changes a score or certification already issued. Scores and levels are versioned; a new version applies to new runs only.
Fuzzy never describes a program as safe or audited. A certification says the build survived these attacks.
Depth weights: branch coverage 40, instruction coverage 20, attack classes tried 20, real state 10, effort 10.
Ceilings: critical 20, high 45, medium 70, low 90, none proven 100.

Certification levels: 1 Sniffed (Sniff or deeper, no proven findings), 2 Fuzzed (Deep Fuzz or deeper on cloned mainnet state, no proven findings), 3 Hardened (Kitchen Sink, no proven findings, score 90 or more).
Run prices in shared Verafy Credits: Sniff 100.

The attack classes: missing signer check, missing owner check, account substitution, PDA seed collision, arithmetic overflow, close then reuse, unchecked CPI target, unchecked mint or authority, lamport draining, reinitialization, price manipulation, compute exhaustion.
